rationale: fftbench is a tiny (6.3 KB text, 11 functions) numeric benchmark dominated by hot inner loops (fft, polynomial multiply/inverse), so runtime cost is the binding constraint: SUB and SPLIT get strong weights because they add arithmetic/structural diversity at near-zero runtime and correctness cost, making them ideal for the tight DSP loops, while FLA and BCF carry deliberately high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.80/0.65 and 0.55/0.70) so the selector applies them sparingly — only to larger, colder functions like the polynomial helpers rather than the FFT kernel. ICALL is down-weighted (SecurityGain 0.45, CorrectnessRisk 0.30) because this code has few indirect-call opportunities and vtable-style indirection in numeric code yields little secrecy for measurable call overhead; IBR is kept mid-range to obscure branch structure in the more complex control-flow functions without taxing the hot path. IGV retains moderate security/diversity weight but a high SizeCost (0.65) since global-variable scrambling inflates a binary that is already small and where data-section growth is the main size risk. Overall the table biases selection toward cheap, safe transforms across all 11 functions, concentrating expensive control-flow obfuscation on the few large non-kernel functions, which preserves benchmark-runtime validity and correctness while still raising static-analysis difficulty.
